targetText: Firstly, the testing of the theoretical dogmas of the Second International in the crucible of the revolutionary struggle of the masses, in the crucible of living practice: that is to say, the restoration of the broken unity between theory and practice, the healing of the rift between them; for only in this way can a truly proletarian party armed with revolutionary theory be created.
summary: Leninism restores the unity of theory and practice against Second International dogmatism.
explanation: The Second International reduced Marxism to dry, academic formulas and parliamentary routine divorced from actual revolutionary struggle. Lenin re-established the vital link between theoretical science and mass action, insisting that all dogma must be tested and forged in the living furnace of practical mass revolution.
context: In August 1914, the dominant leaders of the Second International abandoned anti-militarist resolutions to vote for national war credits in World War I, prompting Lenin to break irrevocably with their reformist opportunism.

targetText: This is why Lenin said that "revolutionary theory is not a dogma," that it "assumes final shape only in close connection with the practical activity of a truly mass and truly revolutionary movement" ("Left-Wing" Communism3); for theory must serve practice, for "theory must answer the questions raised by practice" (What the "Friends of the People" Are 4), for it must be tested by practical results.
summary: Marxist theory is not a rigid dogma, but a living guide to mass revolutionary action.
explanation: Theory assumes definitive scientific shape only in unbreakable connection with the concrete struggles of the working masses. Theory must answer the questions raised by practice, and practice must be enlightened by revolutionary theory.
